clue.text: Losing our tempers about one is shameful

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, that is around, the single letter
to temper is to mix or modify, so these words are blended into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone admits that blowing up at a single person was disgraceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tempers' looks like a noun for bad moods but is the anagram signal: LOSING OUR is rearranged to INGLOROUS, and 'about' wraps it round I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Something without glory brings disgrace, so it is a synonym of shameful.

clue.text: One's cross, having to hold live animal

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to live is to be, to exist
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone is angry because they have to keep a creature alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is the letter X; 'to hold' puts BE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain goat of the Alps is a wild animal.

clue.text: Song to be feature in single, evidently

indicators.note: the letters feature inside the run of the words that follow, held within them

explanation.surface: A track that appears on a single, plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature in' signals that the answer runs across sinGLE Evidently.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song for unaccompanied voices, traditionally for men, is a type of song.

clue.text: Rare odic tribute to male's incidental remark

indicators.note: rare meaning unusual or strange signals that these letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: An unusual tribute about the odic force is paid to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' is the anagram signal: ODIC TRIBUTE becomes OBITERDICTU, and M (male) completes it. 'odic' refers to a supposed natural force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means a thing said in passing, a judge's aside not binding as precedent.

clue.text: Victor, abandoned by women, is taking heart?

indicators.note: the victor word is left without the letter for women, which deserts it

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A champion, dumped by the ladies, is plucking up courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a name, or the V of the radio alphabet, but means WINNER; dropping W leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its central, innermost part.

clue.text: Not cast down holding animal to be lacking injury

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: feathers that have not been cast off are down left unshed
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Someone who is not dejected, carrying a pet, has come through unharmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cast down' suggests cheerful, but here down means soft feathers, and feathers not cast off by a moulting bird are unshed; 'holding' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Escaping without harm means coming through without hurt, so it means uninjured.

clue.text: Crave some bitchiness

indicators.note: only some of the letters in the word that follows are used

explanation.surface: Longing for a bit of spitefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals that the answer sits within bITCHiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To have an itch for something is to long for it, so the verb means crave.

clue.text: Ditch firm by getting personal cover?

parts.note: a ditch is a trench
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
by, as in at a place, gives at

explanation.surface: Get rid of a company by obtaining your own insurance policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' reads as a verb, abandon, but is the noun TRENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A raincoat in military style covers its wearer, a garment being personal cover.

clue.text: Effect of too many higher degrees?

definitions.text: Effect of too many higher degrees?

parts.words: Effect of too many higher degrees?
parts.note: higher degrees suggest academic qualifications, but they are degrees of temperature; too many cause a collapse from heat

explanation.surface: Getting too many postgraduate qualifications has a harmful result.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapse from overheating results when the body's temperature climbs too high.

clue.text: Detective has intelligence to get point of observer

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
wit is intelligence
a ness is a headland or point

explanation.surface: A sleuth uses brains to understand what a watcher means.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland, found in British place names such as Dungeness on the Kent coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saw an event at first hand is an observer of it.

clue.text: Blood products would be returned to Mars

indicators.note: returned means the name of the war god is read backwards

parts.note: Ares is the Greek counterpart of the Roman war god Mars

explanation.surface: Samples of blood would be sent back to the planet Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' suggests the planet but is the god, Greek ARES, turned round by 'would be returned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Serum separated from blood is a blood product; these are its plural.

clue.text: One said to swear after rage is effectively a belligerent

indicators.note: the trooper part comes after the rage part

parts.note: to storm is to rage
people are said to swear like a trooper, a cavalry soldier

explanation.surface: Someone who curses after losing their temper is in effect quarrelsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swear like a trooper' is an idiom for cursing a lot, so the trooper is the one said to swear.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of a Nazi assault unit was an aggressive fighter, a belligerent.

clue.text: Forceful leads of one of red suit causes complaints

parts.note: a heart is a card of one of the two red suits
attacks are forceful leads, as an attack leads the play in a game

explanation.surface: A powerful opening by a player in red gives rise to grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' means medical conditions here, not grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an illness, and a cardiac seizure is a serious one.

clue.text: Awfully nice lector might not need such aids?

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly arranged and must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A very pleasant reader might not need gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' reads as very, but it is the anagram signal for NICE LECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A good reader, a lector, might manage without screens and gadgets, the kind of aids powered by circuits.

clue.text: Like my backing of verse that's unbalanced

parts.note: like means as

indicators.note: backing means the word my is turned round

parts.note: metric describes verse written in metre

explanation.surface: Like my support for poetry that is lopsided.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsided, with sides that do not match, is the opposite of symmetrical.

clue.text: Perhaps end of ten country's final stand

definitions.text: Perhaps end of ten country's final stand

parts.words: Perhaps end of ten country's final stand
parts.note: in the flat drained fenland the final channel at its edge would be its closing trench, and the phrase is also a desperate final defence

explanation.surface: Fenland's people make a desperate defence at its border.
explanation.walkthrough: The fens are low drained land in eastern England crossed by ditches.
explanation.definitionFit: A final desperate attempt or stand is made when there is nowhere left to retreat.

clue.text: After short time request church dedicated body

indicators.note: the request comes after the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ask is to request
dedicated to something is being for it
CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: After a brief wait, ask a church to devote itself to a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A group formed for a specific purpose is a body of people.

clue.text: Come up again about mongrel

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Bring up the subject of a stray dog once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen again is to come up again.

clue.text: Commander-in-Chief secures honour, which is funny

indicators.note: the commander's letters secure, or enclose, the honour

parts.note: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A general receives a decoration, which is amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amusing that makes you laugh is humorous.

clue.text: Divert team with song on CD?

parts.note: a side is a team
each song on a CD is a track

explanation.surface: A team distracted by a song on a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off course onto a side issue is to distract or divert.

clue.text: Her misplaced suspicion on land agent could be a minus

indicators.note: the letters are put out of place, giving a rearrangement

parts.note: sus is slang for suspicion
in Scotland a factor is an estate's land agent

explanation.surface: Her mistaken suspicions about the estate manager could be a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges HER SUS into RHESUS. 'a minus' suggests a drawback but means a negative blood group.
explanation.definitionFit: The blood antigen is either present or absent, so a person can be negative for it.

clue.text: Untouchables, say, in Dae ca's territory

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lower-class people live in the region around Dacca.
explanation.walkthrough: Dacca is the old spelling of Dhaka, capital of Bangladesh; the answer runs across dacCA'S TErritory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Untouchables were the lowest hereditary class in Hindu society, an example of a social group.

clue.text: Are able to gather 50 relatives?

indicators.note: the first word gathers the numeral into its middle

parts.note: are able means can
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Can fifty family members get together?
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish tribe of families sharing a name are relatives.

clue.text: Man, say, lies down

indicators.note: down here means knocked over, so the letters fall into another order

explanation.surface: A man is lying down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Anything but marine standard

parts.note: no, the reverse of anything, gives no
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Any standard other than a naval one.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual pattern or standard.

clue.text: Elsie prays for cure of illness

indicators.note: a cure treats something, so the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: Elsie prays that a sickness may be healed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterial skin infection with red swelling is an illness.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot male bird

explanation.surface: A man readies his gun on a rooster.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a gun's hammer readies it to fire; a rooster is a male chicken.

clue.text: Policy with regard to cheque, we hear?

definitions.text: Policy with regard to cheque, we hear?

parts.words: Policy with regard to cheque, we hear?
parts.note: a cheque sounds like a check, a restraint, so a policy of holding enemies in check is meant

explanation.surface: A bank's rules about payments by cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Military policy of discouraging attack by threat of retaliation keeps enemies in check.
